topics.name: Subject and predicate (verb agrees with the real subject)
Relative pronouns who, which, whose, that

questions.prompt: Which is a complete sentence with a subject and a predicate?
options: Worked with a bookbinder all day.
Faraday with a bookbinder all day.
Faraday worked with a bookbinder.
questions.rule: A sentence needs a subject (Faraday) and a predicate with a verb (worked with a bookbinder).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The lecture had started before Faraday arrived.
The lecture had start before Faraday arrived.
The lecture has started before Faraday arrived.
questions.rule: The earlier past action takes the past perfect: had + past participle = had started.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: building
built
builds

questions.rule: Passive = was/were + past participle: was built.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: whom
whose
which

questions.rule: Use which for things (a book) and who for people.

questions.before: The notes of the young man
options: was
were
is
questions.rule: The subject is the notes (plural), not 'the young man', so use were.

questions.before: When Faraday reached the hall, the lecture had already
options: began
begin
begun
questions.rule: After had, use the past participle: had begun (begin - began - begun).
Passive: subject + was sent (was + past participle).

chat: Did you see the start of the science show?
options: No, it had already started when I got there.
No, it had already start when I got there.
No, it has already started when I got there.
questions.rule: The show started before you reached, so use the past perfect: had already started.

chat: How were the drawings at the science fair?
options: The drawings of the magnets were beautiful.
The drawings of the magnets was beautiful.
The drawings of the magnets is beautiful.
questions.rule: The subject is the drawings (plural), so the verb is were.

questions.source: Faraday bound the notes into a book.
options: The notes was bound into a book by Faraday.
The notes were bound into a book by Faraday.
The notes were binded into a book by Faraday.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: were + past participle. Bind - bound - bound; 'notes' is plural, so were.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct relative pronoun.
options: Maxwell was a physicist which knew advanced mathematics.
Maxwell was a physicist who knew advanced mathematics.
Maxwell was a physicist whose knew advanced mathematics.
questions.rule: Maxwell is a person, so use who. Whose must be followed by a noun.

options: Bavarian glass was use in telescopes and microscopes.
Bavarian glass were used in telescopes and microscopes.
Bavarian glass was used in telescopes and microscopes.
questions.rule: Passive: was + past participle (used). 'Glass' is uncountable, so use was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: written
writing
writes

questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: write - wrote - written.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: who
whose
which

questions.rule: A glass brick is a thing and it is the subject of 'reminded', so use which. Whom is only for people.

options: who
whose
which
questions.rule: Whose shows possession: the boy's speech = the boy whose speech.

options: is
be
are
questions.rule: Simple present passive: are + past participle. 'Motors' is plural, so are used.
By noon + past perfect: the work was finished before that time - had bound.

options: He was a chemist which gave famous lectures.
He was a chemist who gave famous lectures.
He was a chemist whom gave famous lectures.
questions.rule: For a person doing the action, use who: a chemist who gave lectures.

questions.source: Davy hired Faraday as his secretary.
options: Faraday is hired by Davy as his secretary.
Faraday was hire by Davy as his secretary.
Faraday was hired by Davy as his secretary.
questions.rule: 'Hired' is simple past, so the passive is was hired. Keep the tense the same.

questions.source: Faraday finished cleaning the lab. Then he tried the experiment.
options: After Faraday has finished cleaning the lab, he tried the experiment.
After Faraday had finished cleaning the lab, he tried the experiment.
After Faraday had finish cleaning the lab, he tried the experiment.
questions.rule: The first action takes the past perfect: After he had finished ..., he tried ...

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence where the verb agrees with its subject.
options: A box of iron filings were kept near the magnet.
A box of iron filings was kept near the magnet.
A box of iron filings are kept near the magnet.
questions.rule: The subject is a box (singular). 'Of iron filings' only describes it, so use was.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: When Davy reached the lab, Faraday had already cleaned it.
When Davy reached the lab, Faraday has already cleaned it.
When Davy reached the lab, Faraday had already clean it.
questions.rule: The cleaning happened first, so use had already cleaned with the simple past reached.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: depend
depending
dependent

questions.rule: The subject has three things joined by and, so it is plural: they all depend.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: giving
gives
given

questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: give - gave - given.

questions.after: lab had exploded, needed an assistant.
options: whose
who
which
questions.rule: Davy's lab = Davy, whose lab. Whose joins a person to what belongs to him.
whose + noun: the chemist whose lectures were famous.
Simple past passive: was built; the time phrase within a few days comes after.

chat: Is the box of magnets in the lab?
options: Yes, the box of magnets is on the top shelf.
Yes, the box of magnets are on the top shelf.
Yes, the box of magnets be on the top shelf.
questions.rule: The subject is the box (singular), so the verb is is.

chat: When was this old microscope bought?
options: It was bought by my grandfather in 1990.
It was buyed by my grandfather in 1990.
It is bought by my grandfather in 1990.
questions.rule: 'In 1990' is past, so use was + past participle: buy - bought - bought.

questions.source: Faraday was a bookbinder. He loved reading.
options: Faraday was a bookbinder who he loved reading.
Faraday was a bookbinder who loved reading.
Faraday was a bookbinder which loved reading.
questions.rule: Who replaces 'he', so do not repeat the pronoun: a bookbinder who loved reading.

options: Davy said that he has saw Faraday's notes.
Davy said that he had saw Faraday's notes.
Davy said that he had seen Faraday's notes.
questions.rule: In reported speech the earlier action goes back to had + past participle: had seen.

options: Maxwell was the most best mathematician that Faraday ever worked with.
Maxwell was the best mathematician that Faraday ever worked with.
Maxwell was the better mathematician that Faraday ever worked with.
questions.rule: After a superlative, that is used; good - better - best, and never 'most best'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: failing
fails
failed

questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had never failed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: which
whose
who

questions.rule: The pronoun is the subject of 'was', so use who. Whom is an object form.

questions.after: studied by students for many years.
options: have been
has been
have
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: have been + past participle. 'Laws' is plural, so have been.

options: are
have
is
questions.rule: The subject is one (singular), not 'notebooks', so use is.
A past perfect question starts with Had: Had you finished ...?

chat: Which book are you reading these days?
options: I am reading a book that tells the story of Faraday.
I am reading a book who tells the story of Faraday.
I am reading a book that tell the story of Faraday.
questions.rule: Use that/which for a thing; 'a book' is singular, so that tells.

options: Faraday's laws were studied by students.
Faraday's laws are studied by students.
Faraday's laws are study by students.
questions.rule: 'Study' is simple present, so the passive is are studied. Keep the tense.

questions.source: Davy said, "I was hurt in an explosion."
options: Davy said that he had been hurt in an explosion.
Davy said that I had been hurt in an explosion.
Davy said that he has been hurt in an explosion.
questions.rule: I becomes he, and the simple past 'was' goes back to had been.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence where the verb agrees with its subject.
options: Each of these discoveries have changed our lives.
Each of these discoveries has changed our lives.
Each of these discoveries were changed our lives.
questions.rule: The subject is each (singular), so use has changed.

options: The scientist who's drawings were rejected never gave up.
The scientist whom drawings were rejected never gave up.
The scientist whose drawings were rejected never gave up.
questions.rule: Whose shows possession (his drawings). Who's means 'who is'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: are
was
been

questions.rule: With as well as, the verb agrees with the first subject, Michael Faraday: was working.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: causing
causes
caused

questions.rule: Passive = were + past participle: were caused by magnetic fields.

questions.after: had been sent for binding, changed Faraday's life.
options: who
whose
which
questions.rule: The pronoun stands for a thing (the book) and is the subject of 'had been sent', so use which.
Passive: subject + were turned + by + the doer (Maxwell).

options: Had Faraday finished the task?
Did Faraday had finished the task?
Has Faraday finished the task?
questions.rule: In a past perfect question, Had comes before the subject: Had Faraday finished ...?

chat: Why were you so late coming home from the science fair?
options: The last bus has left by the time we finished packing.
The last bus had left by the time we finished packing.
The last bus had leave by the time we finished packing.
questions.rule: The bus left before you finished, so use had left (leave - left - left).

chat: Is the volcano model ready for tomorrow?
options: Yes, it was finished by Kabir last night.
Yes, it was finish by Kabir last night.
Yes, it is finished by Kabir last night.
questions.rule: 'Last night' is past, so use the past passive: was finished.

questions.source: The secret was never learnt by Faraday.
options: Faraday never learnt the secret.
Faraday never learns the secret.
Faraday never learnt by the secret.
questions.rule: The doer (Faraday) becomes the subject and the tense stays simple past: Faraday never learnt the secret.
